description: R08 TerminalApp JsonUtils family checkpoint: the shared terminal-settings JSON conversion owner reproduces all 13 Microsoft JsonUtilsTests contracts, including Missing/Null/Value semantics, filling overloads, custom converters, enum/flag maps, nested key errors, hstring-like null handling and double optional serialization.

entries.notes: JsonConversion reproduces bare/optional type mismatch, null and successful returning semantics.
Filling converts into temporary storage first, preserving the destination on errors and distinguishing optional null.
Keyed returning preserves Microsoft's Missing versus Null behavior for bare and optional values.
Keyed filling reports absent members without modifying storage and annotates conversion errors with the key.
Portable conversions cover strings, signed/unsigned integers, bool, float/double, wide strings, RGB shorthand/canonicalization and GUID validation/roundtrip.
JsonConverter supports temporary and stateful caller-provided converters for direct and keyed reads.
User-defined JsonConversion implementations participate in direct and keyed conversion.
EnumMapper handles known names, rejects unknown values and serializes mapped enum values.
FlagMapper reproduces single/array mappings, none/all sentinels, composition, serialization and invalid combinations.
Conversion errors raised below keyed lookup retain the failing member key.
Nullable string-like values serialize empty as null, populated as strings and absent outer optionals as omitted members.
A conversion type that accepts null maps it to a concrete empty value, including inside Option, while missing keys remain no-ops.
Nested Option preserves all three states: member absent, member present/null and member present/value on serialization and keyed filling.
